inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,866 logical lines, including front matter, every proof section and appendix, page artifacts, references, and affiliation. The article supplies 25 materially distinct units: the random-unitary bridge for shifted moments; the 1/log T correlation transition; tail-measure and prime-covariance upper-bound machinery; Dirichlet-polynomial, Euler-product, residue, and diagonal-dominance lower-bound machinery; and collision/graph arguments that make limiting constants and negligible residues rigorous. The text layer often degrades displayed products, superscripts, and subscripts, but the selected mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose; exact symbolic reuse requires comparison with the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: Characteristic-polynomial moments model zeta moments after matrix-size scaling
accepted_units.why_material: The source replaces critical-line values by characteristic polynomials of random unitary matrices, computes their moment growth, and then transfers the matrix-size exponent and Barnes-G factor to a zeta-moment conjecture with a separate arithmetic factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 29-46 supply the classical moment problem and known upper/lower background; this unit begins where the new representation is introduced.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependency: the bridge and scaling are explicit in prose, while the Barnes-G quotient and Euler product should be checked against the PDF before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Shifted moments split into coalesced, critical-scale, and separated regimes
accepted_units.why_material: The multishift moment definition makes relative shifts the semantic variables, and Conjecture 1 predicts a change from fully correlated growth to separated growth when the relative displacement crosses the inverse logarithmic scale.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the admissible shift behavior, the connection to the general moment recipe and Kosters's critical scaling, and all three stated regimes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency for exact powers and constants; the three-way regime distinction is recoverable from prose and displayed cases, but subscripts and fractions need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: A shifted-moment upper bound is reduced to a joint log-zeta tail set
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1.1 encodes pairwise shift interactions through capped inverse separations, then generalizes Soundararajan's tail-distribution method from one log-zeta value to a weighted sum of shifted log-zeta values.
accepted_units.context_note: The span contains the theorem, definition of the joint exceptional set, the layer-cake identity motivating it, and the stated point of departure from the single-shift proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The reduction is prose-stable; exact exponents in the theorem and the extracted integral notation require PDF comparison.

accepted_units.title: The unconditional lower bound reproduces the pairwise separation factors
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1.2 shows that, for integer weights and controlled shifts, the same capped inverse-separation structure appearing in the conditional upper bound is also forced from below.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the extra hypotheses and the parameter beta recording the finite critical-scale clusters.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent for the exact product and powers; statement structure and hypotheses are legible, with exact typography to be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A short Dirichlet-polynomial proxy turns a moment lower bound into an energy quotient
accepted_units.why_material: The zeta-product is approximated by a short coefficient polynomial A(t); a smoothed correlation S1 and its quadratic energy S2 are combined by Cauchy-Schwarz so the desired moment is bounded below by S1 squared over S2.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes the construction of A(t), the smoothing assumptions, the Cauchy-Schwarz quotient, and the two estimates that complete the route.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependency: the quotient mechanism is clear, but the convolution coefficients and exponents should be verified from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Matching bounds identify the inverse-logarithmic correlation transition
accepted_units.why_material: The source compares the two-shift upper and lower orders in the finite and infinite scaled-separation cases, interpreting their change as a transition from correlated to asymptotically independent value distributions.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the paper's explicit synthesis of Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 rather than an inference imported from the abstract.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-to-moderate: the prose states the transition, although the extracted 1/log T fraction and moment exponents should be checked visually.

accepted_units.title: The shifted unitary integral exhibits the same three separation regimes
accepted_units.why_material: Translation invariance reduces two matrix arguments to their difference, and Proposition 2.1 separates coincident, finite scaled, and widely separated shifts, supplying the random-matrix model for Conjecture 1.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the shifted characteristic-polynomial integral, reduction to one relative angle, zeta/matrix scaling, the three cases, and provenance of the finite-scale case.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency for constants, powers, and the determinant ratio; the regime architecture is clear but exact symbols require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Coalescing shifts merge two insertions into a higher moment
accepted_units.why_material: A contour identity is rescaled by the matrix size; when the shift is smaller than the inverse matrix scale, both pole families coalesce and the normalized shifted integral becomes the ordinary moment with doubled multiplicity.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes the reusable contour identity, the shifted contour representation, the small-separation change of variables, and the limiting identification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High contour-formula dependency and extraction risk in products and pole powers; the limiting mechanism is supported by prose, but exact integrands need the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Separated pole families are dominated by balanced contour allocations
accepted_units.why_material: For separation larger than the inverse matrix scale, each contour is split around two pole families. Power counting shows that only allocations with equal numbers assigned to each family survive at leading order, causing factorization into two ordinary moments times a separation factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes contour decomposition, rescaling, the balance claim, symmetry reduction, factorization, and the minimization that proves dominance.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependency: prose preserves the allocation and minimization logic, but the contour products and power counts must be verified against the original PDF.

accepted_units.title: Finite scaled separation is encoded by a continuous determinant limit
accepted_units.why_material: At nonzero finite matrix-scaled separation, the same rescaling leads to a sine-kernel determinant divided by a Vandermonde factor; continuous extension defines the interpolation constant between the two extreme regimes.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit states the critical-scale case and explicitly defers existence of the collision limit to Appendix 5.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency for the determinant and limiting variables; exact notation requires PDF checking, while the continuous-extension role is explicit.

accepted_units.title: A covariance parameter controls Gaussian and large-deviation tails
accepted_units.why_material: The moment is written as an integral of joint-tail measure, and Theorem 3.1 packages all shift interaction into W, giving Gaussian-like decay through the moderate range and stronger exponential decay for extreme values.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the layer-cake identity, definition of W, all three tail regimes, the cruder form actually needed, and the implication for Theorem 1.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent for numerical thresholds and correction factors; the change of tail behavior and role of W are recoverable, with constants needing PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The joint log-zeta tail is reduced to two prime ranges
accepted_units.why_material: An RH upper bound for log-zeta and high moments of prime polynomials are applied to every shift. Prime powers are discarded, and the prime sum is split at a scale chosen so an exceptional value must occur in either a short covariance-bearing block or a longer sparse block.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the quoted analytic inputs, their shifted weighted combination, the parameter choices, the two prime sums, and the exceptional-set dichotomy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency for weights and scale choices; the two-block reduction is explicit in prose, but exact coefficients and inequalities require PDF comparison.

accepted_units.title: Oscillation caps prime covariance at the inverse shift scale
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 3.5 bounds the prime cosine covariance by the logarithm of the smaller of the prime cutoff and inverse displacement, explaining directly why nearby shifts correlate and separated shifts stop accumulating covariance.
accepted_units.context_note: The span contains the lemma and its two-case proof via the prime harmonic sum and partial summation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependency; the cutoff argument is prose-stable, while the exact logarithmic expression should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Adaptive moment orders convert prime covariance into exceptional-set decay
accepted_units.why_material: High-moment estimates bound the long and short prime blocks differently; choosing moment order according to V and W yields the Gaussian core and very-large-value tail needed for the shifted moment bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 3.6, both moment estimates, the optimized choices, and the conclusion of Theorem 3.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency for admissible moment orders and exponents; the optimization mechanism is clear but exact thresholds require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The short polynomial's mean square already contains the full shift-correlation product
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 4.1 identifies the mean square of A(t) with the same pairwise capped inverse-separation factors as the target moment, reducing the analytic lower bound to understanding a multiplicative coefficient norm.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the section hypotheses, lemma statement, dyadic reduction, and the exact coefficient-square expression that begins the proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency for convolution coefficients and exponents; the mean-square reduction is recoverable, with exact normalization requiring PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Shifted coefficient energy becomes a product of displaced zeta singularities
accepted_units.why_material: Multiplicativity turns the coefficient-square Dirichlet series into one central zeta factor and one conjugate pair for every shift difference, with a holomorphic Euler factor. This exposes correlation as the geometry of clustered singularities.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the multiplicative coefficient definition, Perron representation, local Euler expansion, and global factorization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependency and product-order extraction risk; the singularity pattern is clear, but exact factor powers need the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Contour shifting separates critical-scale pole clusters from remote residues
accepted_units.why_material: A truncated Perron integral is moved into a zero-free region. The main pole at zero and poles whose shift differences lie within the inverse-logarithmic scale are retained, while residues at more distant displacement poles are isolated as a negligible term to be proved later.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes truncation control, the contour rectangle, the residue decomposition, definitions of the close and far index sets, and the remote-residue claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency for contour errors and residue orders; the close/far classification is prose-grounded, with exact estimates needing PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: One small contour captures a whole critical-scale singularity cluster
accepted_units.why_material: The residues at zero and all inverse-logarithmically close shift poles are enclosed by one shrinking circle. Laurent expansions show that analytic or lower-pole-order terms integrate away or are lower order, leaving the product of the principal singular parts.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the small-circle construction, expansion, vanishing argument, two required bounds, and the local zeta estimates that justify them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependency; the cluster principle and cancellation are explicit, but exact Laurent powers and index products require PDF comparison.

accepted_units.title: Coefficient and analyticity bounds suppress every correction to the main clustered residue
accepted_units.why_material: The principal cluster integral is expanded into separation coefficients and Taylor coefficients of an analytic remainder. Bounds from combinatorial coefficient growth and radius of convergence show that only the first series contributes at leading order, recovering the pairwise min-factor asymptotic.
accepted_units.context_note: The span contains the series decomposition, coefficient estimates, treatment of all four sums, and the conclusion of Lemma 4.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependency and OCR risk across multi-line series; the dominance argument is recoverable from prose, but exact series and constants need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Mellin inversion gives a uniform smoothed Dirichlet approximation to the shifted zeta product
accepted_units.why_material: The full product is represented by a smoothed coefficient series; shifting the Mellin contour leaves the value at zero plus clustered pole residues, while gamma decay and a partition of near-coincident shifts make all extra terms uniformly negligible.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the coefficient/product definitions, Lemma 4.2, Mellin inversion, contour shift, analytic bounds, pole clustering, and the final approximation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency for smoothing exponents and residue locations; the contour mechanism is prose-stable, with exact normalization requiring the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Fourier localization kills off-diagonal correlations and preserves coefficient energy
accepted_units.why_material: Substituting the smoothed approximation into S1 converts it to a double coefficient sum weighted by the Fourier transform of a compactly supported cutoff. Rapid decay makes off-diagonal terms negligible, while the positive diagonal is exactly the coefficient energy from Lemma 4.1.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 4.3, approximation error control, diagonal/off-diagonal split, Fourier decay, and the resulting lower bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency for transforms and truncation scales; positivity and diagonal dominance are clear, but exact factors need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Repeated divided differences cancel the Vandermonde singularity
accepted_units.why_material: Appendix 5.1 proves existence of the critical-scale constant by expressing the sine kernel through an even analytic function and repeatedly subtracting/dividing rows and columns, extracting exactly the squared Vandermonde factors before points coalesce.
accepted_units.context_note: This closes the existence claim deferred at line 518 and includes the limiting derivative matrix.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High determinant-formula dependency; the divided-difference procedure is explicit, but matrix dimensions and derivative indices should be verified against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Remote residue bounds require a partition by relative shift geometry
accepted_units.why_material: To prove remote poles negligible, the appendix groups poles near a chosen remote difference and divides every other pair into close, dominant-scale, separated-scale, or near-parallel-difference cases, producing a target exponent inequality.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the residue cluster V0, local zeta bounds, the V1/V2/V3 partition, and reduction of negligibility to inequality (35).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula and set-notation dependency; the case geometry is prose-recoverable, while exact exponent bookkeeping requires PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: A signed bipartite graph turns residue exponent positivity into component squares
accepted_units.why_material: The first exponent inequality is encoded by a bipartite graph on positive and negative weights. Structural properties forbid sign-paired cycles and force a singleton component, so a sum of squared component weights is strictly positive and dominates the required exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the graph definition, proofs of its five properties, and the component-square derivation of inequality (36).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependency: the graph logic is prose-stable, while the exact weighted exponent identity should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Nested shift scales extend graph positivity to all near-parallel differences
accepted_units.why_material: The remaining near-parallel shift differences are organized into asymptotic equivalence classes. A nested family of graphs repeats the positivity argument at each scale, and induction across their strict hierarchy proves the final negligible-residue estimate.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the equivalence relation, scale representatives, enlarged graphs, inherited properties, inequalities at each scale, and the induction closing (35).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula/set dependency in the final induction; the multiscale graph mechanism is clear, but exact products and exponents require PDF verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One shift scale appears in matrix, prime, and Euler-singularity coordinates
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The inverse-logarithmic transition is represented three ways: matrix pole separation at inverse matrix size, cessation of accumulated prime covariance, and separation of shifted zeta singularities in the coefficient Euler product.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The matrix statement is conjectural evidence for zeta asymptotics, while the zeta results are bounds under different hypotheses; the representations should not be treated as one proved equivalence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Upper bounds flow from covariance to tails to moments
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Pairwise oscillatory covariance determines W, W controls the high-value tail of the weighted shifted log-zeta sum, and integrating that tail produces the shifted-moment upper bound.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This pipeline assumes RH and gives an upper bound with an epsilon loss, not the conjectured asymptotic.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Lower bounds flow from a proxy's energy to a localized diagonal
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The short Dirichlet polynomial stores the pairwise shift geometry in its coefficient energy; smoothing and Fourier localization recover that energy as a positive diagonal correlation, and Cauchy-Schwarz transfers it to the zeta moment.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The argument requires positive integer weights and the paper's stated shift-size conditions, so it does not match the full real-weight scope of the upper bound.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Coalescing singularities are handled by local compression before taking limits
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Both the random-matrix and Dirichlet-series analyses first enclose a cluster of nearby singularities as one object; rescaling, Laurent extraction, or divided differences then produce a finite limit without treating colliding poles independently.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The contour integrals and determinant quotient live in different calculations; this is a shared conceptual move, not an identity between their local constants.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Graph positivity certifies that nonprincipal residue scales lose
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After residues are divided into critical and remote scale classes, signed bipartite component structure supplies a positive exponent gap; nested graphs propagate that gap through every intermediate asymptotic scale.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The certification depends on the prescribed limiting relations among the shifts and proves negligibility only in this residue comparison.
